summary: Deployed inventory-api as a systemd-managed service on node1 (RHEL 9) with OOMScoreAdjust=-1000 so the kernel OOM killer will not select it. Verified end-to-end under a real system-wide OOM: with swap disabled, a hog process was driven to ~1.8GB RSS on a 1.9GB-RAM box; the kernel oom-killer killed the hog while inventory-api (PID 1602, unchanged) stayed active and kept answering /healthz and /inventory. Swap was restored afterward. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured pre-restart boot_id and healthy service state, issued systemctl reboot asynchronously so the exec ack returned first, polled until node1 was reachable again, confirmed a new boot_id proving an actual restart, and confirmed inventory-api auto-started (fresh PID, enabled, OOMScoreAdjust=-1000 intact) and served correct inventory data post-reboot.
actions_performed: Inspected node1: RHEL 9.8, 1.9GiB RAM, 2GiB swap, root access confirmed
Wrote /opt/inventory-api/app.py, a minimal threaded HTTP API serving /healthz and /inventory on port 8080
Created /etc/systemd/system/inventory-api.service with Restart=always, OOMScoreAdjust=-1000, MemoryHigh/MemoryMax; enabled and started it
Verified baseline health via curl and confirmed oom_score_adj=-1000 / oom_score=0 on the running PID
Lightly protected the exec management path (vsock socat listener and sshd) with oom_score_adj=-500 as an independent-recovery safeguard
Disabled swap temporarily (swapoff -a) to reach a genuine system-wide OOM condition quickly and reversibly
Launched a memory-hog Python process that grew RSS to ~1.8GB, driving the system out of memory
Captured dmesg evidence that the kernel OOM killer selected and killed the hog process (pid 1721), not inventory-api
Confirmed inventory-api remained active with the same MainPID and kept serving /healthz and /inventory after the OOM event
Restored swap (swapon -a) back to its original 2GB/0-used state and cleaned up hog script/log files
Captured pre-restart boot_id and confirmed inventory-api active/enabled with live curl checks
Issued systemctl reboot via a backgrounded/disowned wrapper so the exec acknowledgement returned before disconnection
Polled node1 until exec access returned and confirmed a new boot_id (post-reboot uptime reset), proving a genuine restart
Confirmed post-restart recovery: inventory-api auto-started (new MainPID), enabled, OOMScoreAdjust=-1000 intact, serving correct /healthz and /inventory data, swap restored to baseline

evidence.requirement: inventory-api runs as a managed (systemd) service with OOM protection configured
evidence.summary: Unit created/enabled/started; MainPID active; OOMScoreAdjust=-1000 confirmed via systemctl show and /proc/<pid>/oom_score_adj (=-1000, oom_score=0)
inventory-api active, curl /healthz and /inventory return correct JSON; baseline free/swap captured

evidence.requirement: Smallest safe reversible disruption representative of an OOM condition, one component at a time, independent recovery path preserved
evidence.summary: swapoff -a (reversible) then a single memory-hog process launched in background; exec/socat and sshd given protective oom_score_adj beforehand so the management path was preserved

evidence.requirement: Kernel actually driven out of memory and oom-killer invoked
evidence.summary: free -h showed memory fully consumed (1.9Gi used / 13Mi available) then dmesg shows 'python3 invoked oom-killer' and 'Out of memory: Killed process 1721 (python3)'

evidence.requirement: The memory hog, not inventory-api, is the process the kernel stops; inventory-api keeps serving
evidence.summary: dmesg confirms pid 1721 (hog) killed; same command shows systemctl is-active inventory-api=active and curl /healthz succeeding immediately after the kill

evidence.requirement: Post-disruption verification: hog gone, inventory-api PID unchanged, service data intact, environment restored
evidence.summary: inventory-api MainPID still 1602 (never restarted), /inventory data correct, no hog process remains, swap restored to 2GiB/0-used baseline

evidence.requirement: Node restart protocol - pre-restart boot identity and health baseline
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id=55595e92-e932-451b-ac1d-75d72072b358, uptime-since, inventory-api active/enabled, and live /healthz + /inventory responses

evidence.requirement: Node restart protocol - safe restart acknowledged before disconnect
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot issued via backgrounded/disowned wrapper returning REBOOT_SCHEDULED immediately; subsequent exec call timed out confirming the node actually went down

evidence.requirement: Node restart protocol - changed boot identity proving genuine restart
evidence.summary: New boot_id=a3b4838e-83a4-4a75-854f-1cdb6ca71534 (different from baseline) and uptime-since reset to 23:45:31, proving a true reboot occurred

evidence.requirement: Node restart protocol - post-restart recovery of required service and data
evidence.summary: inventory-api auto-started with new MainPID=725, enabled, OOMScoreAdjust=-1000 intact, /healthz and /inventory serving correct data, swap back at 2GiB/0-used
